Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Denominations and Characteristics of Coins
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denomination and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 3rd December 2004 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year date “2004” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock of the coin.
Balestier, Jalan Besar, Joo Chiat and Tanjong Katong exude the old world charm of Singapore’s yesteryears, with rich architectural heritage, thriving street life and unique streetscapes.
Balestier
The centre features the façade of a shophouse with very distinctive rich plaster relief (in full colour for the silver coin), reflecting the heritage of the Chinese community in this area. On the right is a typical spiral staircase associated with the shophouses in the vicinity. At the top is the Balestier Market built in the 1920s for locals to sell their produce. It was also a centre for the distribution of food ration during World War II.
The bottom depicts the only remaining permanent freestanding wayang stage in mainland Singapore. It was built in 1906 and belongs to the Go Chor Tua Pek Kong Temple.

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2004” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin.
Jalan Besar
The centre features the distinctive Art-Deco street frontage and exposed brickwork (in full colour for the silver coin). This area has a very distinct historic streetscape along Serangoon Road and Lavender Street. At the top is a row of shophouses with special corner treatments that are distinctive to the area. The right depicts the typical ornate bracket that supports the upper storey verandah. The bottom showcases the original wooden windows of the conservation shophouses in the area.
Joo Chiat
The centre features the colourful Peranakan shophouse frontage featuring patterned tiles and rich
plasterworks (in full colour for the silver coin). At the top is the Katong Red House Bakery, a distinctive
landmark in the area that used to serve traditional bread and pastries since 1925 till it closed recently for conservation. The right depicts the typical swing door (pintu-pagar) of the entrance of the conservation shop houses in the area. The bottom features a row of conservation shophouses with elaborate windows and façade details reflecting the colourful culture of the Peranakan community residing in this area.
Tanjong Katong
The centre features the unique balconies of a row
of shophouses in the Tanjong Katong area (in full colour for the silver coin). At the top is the former Tanjong Katong Girls’ School Hall,
a landmark of the area. The right depicts an elegantly-designed column from one of the shophouses in the area. The bottom features the Tanjong Katong Post Office. Built in the 1920-1930s, its use continues even today, serving the residents in the area.
The denomination of the coin in figures is to the left of the main design on all the coins.
